scenes.say: Redwood River's new warehouse worker earns a thousand dollars a week. But her paycheck says seven hundred fifty-eight fifty. Where did the rest go?

sub: hours × rate, or salary, plus overtime
scenes.say: Gross pay is total earnings before anything is taken out: hours worked times the hourly rate, or a salary, plus any overtime or bonuses. Federal law requires overtime at one and a half times the regular rate for hours over forty a week for most hourly workers.
Net pay is what the employee actually takes home after every deduction.

scenes.heading: One week's pay
scenes.say: Here's the week. Gross pay one thousand. Less federal income tax ninety, Minnesota income tax forty-five, Social Security sixty-two, Medicare fourteen fifty, and her share of health insurance thirty. Net pay: seven hundred fifty-eight fifty.

scenes.big: The employer holds it in trust
sub: paid to the government or insurer
scenes.say: The amounts withheld don't belong to Redwood River. It holds them for the government and the insurer, so each one is a liability until it's paid over.

scenes.q: Gross pay $800, total deductions $190. Net pay?
scenes.say: Quick check. Gross pay eight hundred, total deductions one ninety. What's net pay? Pause and pick.
Some deductions are required by law. Others the employee chooses. Here are the main ones on every US paycheck.

scenes.heading: Required by law
items: Federal income tax: based on Form W-4
Social Security: 6.2% up to an annual limit
scenes.say: Required by law: federal income tax, based on the elections the employee makes on Form W-4. State income tax, which Minnesota requires employers to withhold. Social Security at six point two percent, on wages up to an annual limit. And Medicare at one point four five percent, on all wages.

Social Security and Medicare together are called FICA taxes, after the Federal Insurance Contributions Act. Combined, that's seven point six five percent. High earners also pay an extra Medicare tax on wages above two hundred thousand dollars.

scenes.heading: Voluntary deductions
scenes.say: Voluntary deductions are ones the employee chooses: their share of health insurance, contributions to a retirement plan like a four oh one k, union dues, and charitable gifts.
For our warehouse worker, FICA is seventy-six fifty: sixty-two for Social Security and fourteen fifty for Medicare.

scenes.q: Gross pay $2,000. Employee's total FICA (no limits reached)?
scenes.say: Quick check. Gross pay is two thousand dollars, and no limits have been reached. What's the employee's total FICA? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, one fifty-three. Two thousand times seven point six five percent.

scenes.say: A thousand dollar wage costs Redwood River more than a thousand dollars. On top of the paycheck, the employer pays its own payroll taxes.

scenes.heading: The employer pays
scenes.say: The employer matches the employee's Social Security and Medicare, dollar for dollar. It also pays federal unemployment tax, called FUTA, and state unemployment tax, called SUTA. Employees don't pay unemployment taxes.

sub: on the first $7,000 of each worker's wages
scenes.say: FUTA is six percent on the first seven thousand dollars of each worker's wages a year. But employers who pay their state unemployment tax on time get a credit of up to five point four percent, so the usual effective rate is just point six percent.

scenes.heading: Employer cost of one week
scenes.note: Minnesota sets each employer's SUTA rate and wage base.
scenes.say: For the warehouse worker's week: sixty-two for the Social Security match, fourteen fifty for Medicare, six for FUTA, and ten for state unemployment, using an illustrative one percent rate. Minnesota sets each employer's actual rate. Total employer payroll tax: ninety-two fifty.
So a one thousand dollar wage really costs Redwood River one thousand ninety-two fifty, before any benefits it provides.

scenes.q: Which tax is paid by BOTH the employee and the employer?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which tax is paid by both the employee and the employer? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, Social Security. Medicare is too. Unemployment taxes fall on the employer, and income tax on the employee.

scenes.say: Every payroll takes two journal entries: one for the employee's pay, and one for the employer's taxes.

scenes.heading: Entry 1 · Wages and withholdings
scenes.say: First, the wages. Debit wages expense for the full gross pay, one thousand. Credit a payable for each withholding: federal income tax ninety, state income tax forty-five, Social Security sixty-two, Medicare fourteen fifty, and health insurance thirty. Credit cash for the net pay, seven fifty-eight fifty.

scenes.heading: Entry 2 · Employer payroll taxes
scenes.say: Second, the employer's taxes. Debit payroll tax expense ninety-two fifty. Credit Social Security payable sixty-two, Medicare payable fourteen fifty, FUTA payable six and SUTA payable ten.
Notice Social Security payable now holds one twenty-four, half from the employee and half from the employer. The two halves are paid to the IRS together.

scenes.heading: Paying the IRS later
scenes.say: When the taxes are deposited, debit each payable and credit cash. The liabilities disappear and no new expense is recorded.

scenes.q: In Entry 1, which account is debited?
scenes.say: Quick check. In the first payroll entry, what's debited? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, wages expense for the full gross pay. The deductions are part of the employee's wage.

scenes.say: Pay isn't just wages. Vacation days, health insurance and retirement contributions are costs too, and they're earned as employees work.

sub: Paid vacation, holidays and sick days
that employees earn as they work
scenes.say: Compensated absences are paid time off, like vacation, holidays and sick leave, that employees earn as they work. Under expense recognition, the cost belongs in the period the time is earned, not when it's taken.

scenes.heading: Accrue vacation each month
scenes.note: Earns 1 day a month; a day's pay is 200.
scenes.say: Redwood River's worker earns one vacation day a month, worth two hundred dollars. Each month, debit vacation benefits expense and credit vacation benefits payable two hundred.

scenes.heading: She takes 3 days in August
scenes.say: When she takes three days off in August, the payable is reduced by six hundred instead of recording a new expense. The cost was already recognized as she earned it.

scenes.heading: Other employer-paid benefits
items: Retirement contributions, such as a 401(k) match
scenes.say: Other benefits paid by the employer, like its share of health insurance, a four oh one k match and workers' compensation insurance, are recorded as expenses with matching liabilities until they're paid.

scenes.q: When is the cost of a vacation day recognized?
opts: At the end of the employee's career
scenes.say: Quick check. When is the cost of a vacation day recognized? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, when it's earned. That's expense recognition at work.

scenes.say: Running payroll means filing forms, on deadlines, with penalties if you're late. Here are the four every employer knows.

scenes.heading: Four key forms
items: W-2: each employee's annual wage statement
scenes.say: Four forms matter most. Form W-4 is completed by each new employee and tells the employer how much federal income tax to withhold. Form 941 is filed every quarter and reports wages, income tax withheld, and both halves of FICA. Form 940 reports federal unemployment tax once a year.

sub: Wages and taxes withheld for the year:
scenes.say: And Form W-2 shows each employee's wages and tax withheld for the year. It must reach employees, and the Social Security Administration, by January thirty-first.
Minnesota has its own filings too: state income tax withholding returns, and quarterly unemployment insurance reports.

Most small businesses, Redwood River included, use a payroll service to calculate, pay and file. But the employer stays legally responsible if anything goes wrong. You'll look at payroll systems again in ACCT 360.

scenes.q: Which form reports each employee's annual wages and tax withheld?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which form reports each employee's annual wages and tax withheld? Pause and pick.
